summary: The Seite Islands' moot: our fathers' banks, defiance or the brokers' judgment, the isle harbours and boats, charter or coves, and the war at sea.

isle_moot_custom.name: The Moot of the Isles
isle_moot_custom.desc: The Seite clans settle every matter at the moot stone, where each fisher has a voice and none a vote that counts for more. It is fair, and it is slow.

moot_stone.name: The Moot Stone
moot_stone.desc: The moot stone is carved with the names of the clans and set on a new platform. Elder Tamsa speaks from it, and fewer arguments go unfinished.

banks_fleet.name: The Banks Fleet
banks_fleet.desc: The fishing boats that guard the banks are fitted with shields at the rail and a signal lamp at the mast. They are not warships, but they are not defenceless.

armed_fishers.name: The Fishing Fleet Armed
armed_fishers.desc: Every boat that works the banks carries spears, nets for fouling an oar and a slinger or two. A fisher who rows to the nets knows how to fight back.

banks_squadron.name: The Banks Flotilla
banks_squadron.desc: The moot's boats sail the banks together in a loose line, hailing each other by lamp. They are many and they are close, and a stranger sees an army.

isles_apart.name: The Isles Keep Apart
isles_apart.desc: The Seite clans pull their boats up the beach and mend their nets while the great crowns fight. The moot has said that this war is no concern of theirs.

seite_petition.title: The Seite Isles Ask Raerby to Judge the Banks
seite_petition.desc: A fishing boat from the Seite Isles has anchored off the council hall, bearing a shell-bound petition from the moot stone. The Seite clans will accept the word of Raerby's captains on the southern banks, and ask whether Raerby will judge between them and Nondondor's king.

shield_request.title: The Seite Isles Ask for a Shield
shield_request.desc: A Seite elder has come to the harbour in a patched boat, with a short speech. The southern banks are in dispute, Nondondor's galleys are many, and the Seite clans have only nets. They ask whether our realm will stand behind them.

focuses.name: The Isle Moot
focuses.desc: The four isles are governed by a moot of fishing clans that meets at a standing stone. Elder Tamsa speaks for it, and decisions are made only when every clan has been heard.

focuses.name: Elders of the Isles
focuses.desc: The oldest fisher of each isle sits at the stone with a staff. They have outlived many kings, and they intend to outlive more.

focuses.name: The Fishers' Voice
focuses.desc: Any fisher may stand at the stone and speak for a count of a hundred. The moot listens, even to those who have nothing to say.

focuses.name: The Moot Stone
focuses.desc: The old stone is raised on a new base, and the names of the clans are cut into it again. The moot meets there each season.

focuses.name: Our Fathers' Banks
focuses.desc: The southern banks have been fished by the Seite clans since before any king claimed them. The moot says so, in its own words, at the start of every season.

focuses.name: Boats on the Banks
focuses.desc: More boats are sent to the banks, each with a lookout and a horn. If any hull comes near, the whole fleet hears of it.

focuses.name: Watch the King's Galleys
focuses.desc: Watch-huts are raised along the southern shore to see the king's galleys coming. A beacon on each can be lit in a breath.

focuses.name: Defy the King
focuses.desc: The moot answers Nondondor's herald with a single sentence: the banks were fished by our fathers and will be fished by our sons. The king is not asked again.

focuses.name: Seek the Brokers' Judgment
focuses.desc: The moot sends a shell-bound petition to Raerby, asking its captains to judge. It would sooner lose a hearing than win a war.

focuses.name: The Banks Fleet
focuses.desc: The moot has the fishing boats fitted out for a fight. They are still fishing boats, and they will fish whenever there is no one to fight.

focuses.name: The Banks Accord
focuses.desc: The banks are shared, and a mark is cut in the moot stone to say so. The Seite clans keep their word, and expect the king to keep his.

focuses.name: Call on Friends
focuses.desc: The moot sends word to every island with a fleet. They ask for friends, not for arms, and they ask politely.

focuses.name: The Isle Harbours
focuses.desc: The best coves of the four isles are cleared of rock and given stone quays. A boat may now land its catch at any state of the tide.

focuses.name: Drying Racks
focuses.desc: Wooden racks line the beaches, hung with split cod and herring. The wind and the sun do the rest, and the clans eat well through the winter.

focuses.name: Boatwrights
focuses.desc: Boatwrights from the four isles are given a common yard and a common supply of timber. They build a better boat in half the time.

focuses.name: The Isle Market
focuses.desc: The isles hold one market, on the beach of the main isle, at the end of each season. Everything from sealskin to fishhooks is for sale.

focuses.name: Stores of Salt Fish
focuses.desc: Barrels of salt-fish are set aside in the moot-house. In a hard year, each clan may draw what it needs, and each must give back in the next.

focuses.name: The Isle Boats
focuses.desc: The long fishing boats are refitted with a second bank of oars and a stronger keel. They are still slow, but they are no longer easy to catch.

focuses.name: The Fishing Fleet Armed
focuses.desc: Every boat that goes to the banks now carries spears and a heavy net. The nets are cast over an enemy's oars, and the spears do the rest.

focuses.name: The Moot's Captain
focuses.desc: The moot gives command of its boats to Captain Brann of the Banks, who has fished there all his life. He knows every rock, and every rock knows him.

focuses.name: The Banks Flotilla
focuses.desc: The moot's boats sail the banks together, hailing each other by lamp and horn. A stranger sees a fleet, and is not far wrong.

focuses.name: The Pupor Question
focuses.desc: The chart houses invite the isles to join a Charter; the coves invite them to profit from the lanes. The moot hears both, and every clan has an opinion.

focuses.name: Join the Pupor Charter
focuses.desc: The moot votes to sign the Pupor Charter, and the elder's mark is cut on the roll. The clans will keep the lanes and take the chart houses' side.

focuses.name: The Free Coves
focuses.desc: The moot opens its quiet coves to any captain who wishes to rest. They ask no questions, and take a tithe of what comes ashore.

focuses.name: The Charter Watch
focuses.desc: Boats from the Seite Isles join the Charter's patrols. They are small, and quick, and know where the corsairs hide.

focuses.name: Cove Raiders
focuses.desc: A few of the fishing clans take to raiding in the lean months. The moot pretends not to see, and collects a fifth.

focuses.name: The War at Sea
focuses.desc: The great fleets have put to sea. The moot meets on the beach at night, and the question before it is whether the isles will stay or sail.

focuses.name: The Isles Keep Apart
focuses.desc: The moot decides that the isles will mend their nets and watch the sea. They have been left alone before, and they will be again.

focuses.name: Boats for the Crossing
focuses.desc: The western host needs small boats for landing and ferrying. The Seite clans have hundreds, and a price for each.

focuses.name: Fishers for the Living
focuses.desc: The stranger has returned, and the clans remember the ship that once begged a harbour from them. They send their best fishers to the coalition, with nets and spears.

focuses.name: A Harbour for Strangers
focuses.desc: The moot lets it be known that any ship may beach on the Seite shore. The clans ask for a small gift, and the gift is always given.

focuses.name: The Fathers Fished Under the League
focuses.desc: Our fathers fished the banks under the league's law, and the league never once put a king over them. The moot says plainly that it will not have one now, whatever the old charts call him.
